feedback.problem:
What is the center of the hyperbola 
$4{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2}-40x+6y=-85?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2}-40x+6y & =-85 \\ 4{x}^{2}-40x-3{y}^{2}+6y & =-85 \\ 4[{x}^{2}-10x]-3[{y}^{2}-2y] & =-85 \\ 4[(x-5)^{2}-25]-3[(y-1)^{2}-1] & =-85 \\ 4(x-5)^{2}-100-3(y-1)^{2}+3 & =-85 \\ 4(x-5)^{2}-3(y-1)^{2} & =12 \\ \frac{(x-5)^{2}}{3}-\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{4} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-5)^{2}}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}}-\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{{2}^{2}} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the center is $(5,1).$
